channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Gerhard Schröder visits latest Russian employer, Hyperglobus
item.description: Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder visited a Moscow supermarket in his new role on the supervisory board. Schröder is no stranger to retirement stipends in Russia — or the scandal that accompanies them.

item.title: [DW] EU enlargement: European Commission tables reforms to prepare bloc for new members
item.description: The European Commission is proposing earlier access to EU markets for candidate countries, new voting rules to reduce vetoes and extra safeguards for a bigger bloc. But is the reform fair — or even feasible?

item.title: [DW] Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
item.description: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.

item.title: [DW] EU pulls sponsorship from Disinfo2026 event in Lithuania
item.description: The EU's diplomatic service, Canada and host nation Lithuania all pulled support from a disinformation event in Vilnius. Amid reports of US pressure, the EU said it was "uncomfortable with the framing" of some panels.

item.title: [DW] Security in the Black Sea region: is Bulgaria the weak link in Europe's defense against threats from Russia?
item.description: Two ships have sunk off the coast of Bulgaria and Romania after drone attacks in recent days. Bulgaria has held back on pointing the finger at Russia. What does that mean for security in the Black Sea and the region?

item.title: [DW] South Korea recalls Ukraine ambassador amid POW dispute
item.description: South Korea has said it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine. Seoul is upset about a transfer of North Korean prisoners of war being made public knowledge at the UN and had demanded — but not received — an apology.

item.title: [DW] As Russia steps up attacks on Ukrainian data centers, could Ukraine soon be offline?
item.description: As Russia targets Ukraine's data centers more and more, experts say the country's internet system is too robust to shut down entirely. However, services could become more expensive.

item.title: [DW] Middle Corridor: Can Bulgaria be a safe gateway for Asian imports to the EU?
item.description: The EU wants more trade via the Middle Corridor, which could bring big benefits for Bulgaria. But Tuesday's drone attacks on commercial ships off the Bulgarian coast are a stark reminder of the security risks involved.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU Parliament’s 7 October memorial honours Israelis, sidelines Palestinians — and sows division
item.description: A memorial to victims of 7 October in Israel, which made no mention of Palestinian casualties, ended in tumbling flags, anger, and grief.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU let member states rewrite targets after they had sought recovery-fund payment, auditors find
item.description: The revised targets were "aligned with actual achieved outputs, which made the payment possible," the auditors wrote in their annual report on last year's budget.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU trade chief Šefčovič has no cards to play on China ‘ultimatum’ trip
item.description: Tough rhetoric aside, the EU cannot threaten China with much if it wants to avoid a tit-for-tat trade war. But a unified position would help.

item.title: [Financial Times] Missile strike on Riyadh airport kills 12 and injures hundreds
item.description: Deadly assault in Saudi Arabia comes days after multiple attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels

item.title: [EU Observer] EU should use Digital Services Act against online tormentors of Belarusian and Russian exiles in Europe
item.description: By treating digital attacks on Belarusian and Russian exiles as a systemic risk under the DSA, the EU could reshape how global platforms handle online transnational repression.

item.title: [DW] Couples looking to have children often turn to surrogacy agencies in Georgia without understanding the hidden costs
item.description: Georgia became a hub for surrogate pregnancies after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. DW spoke with parents, and those who wanted to become parents, about the hidden costs of a booming industry.

item.title: [Financial Times] India’s ‘Cockroach’ leaders released as movement calls for more protests
item.description: Abhijeet Dipke of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party was let go by a court order as police tightened security in New Delhi

item.title: [DW] Ukrainian prisoners of war and defectors have been gathered into a Russian battalion to face Ukrainian forces — why? And how?
item.description: Russia has announced a battalion consisting of Ukrainian "volunteers." But veterans and former prisoners of war share very different accounts.

item.title: [Financial Times] US hits commercial tanker in Gulf of Oman as tensions flare
item.description: The ship tried to break through America’s naval blockade of Iranian ports, Central Command says of its first attack in a month

item.title: [Financial Times] US justice department probes TV networks over Trump pool coverage
item.description: ABC News, CBS News, CNN, Fox News and NBC News refused to cover the president’s activities after last month’s White House ban

item.title: [Financial Times] The problem with your AI therapist
item.description: Millions are turning to chatbots for help with mental health but a technology that can’t go beyond words won’t heal them

item.title: [Financial Times] The fall of Germany’s ex-spymaster
item.description: August Hanning is accused of having illegally purchased state secrets for over a decade

item.title: [Financial Times] Why are our children not flourishing at school?
item.description: AI is detonating the tired system of factory education that has predominated since the last century

item.title: [Financial Times] Russia steps up bid to kill European defence chiefs, spy agencies warn
item.description: Companies increase personal security for top executives as Kremlin orders expansion of sabotage and ‘hybrid’ operations

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump is failing to arrest decline in popularity, FT poll shows
item.description: Voters increasingly doubt the president’s ability to steer the economy with weeks to go until elections

item.title: [Financial Times] China’s growing debt burden limits space for economic stimulus
item.description: Mounting interest payments restrict headroom to revive domestic demand, say experts

item.title: [Politico Europe] Security Sunday: Europas Krieg der Zukunft — mit Nico Lange
item.description: Fast jede Nacht überzieht Russland die Ukraine mit Drohnen- und Raketenangriffen, um die Zivilbevölkerung zu zermürben. Doch abseits des Terrors aus der Luft kommt Moskau militärisch kaum voran. Die wahre Strategie des Kremls zielt längst auf ein anderes Schlachtfeld: die politische Erschöpfung Europas und der USA. Im Gespräch mit POLITICO-Reporterin Rixa Fürsen teilt Nico Lange, […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Russians face EU travel curbs to prevent hybrid attacks
item.description: Tighter visa rules are expected to be proposed in January to bolster EU defenses against Russian threats.

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump tells Ukraine to ‘get a new leader’ as US threatens to cut off intelligence-sharing
item.description: US officials step up pressure on Kyiv to stop striking Russian oil refineries after Trump cut diesel deal with Putin

item.title: [Politico Europe] Germany warns EU that €159B budget cuts are not enough
item.description: Frugal countries said an end-of-year agreement is less likely after Ireland's proposal.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] France school protests go deeper than rioting or reactionism, says Sciences Po lecturer
item.description: Professor Jan Rovný argues French school protests could turn into a movment against spending cuts by a government with growing debt. He explains why private school pupils have joined publicly educated peers revolting on the streets, and how police violence will shape public mood.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Strikes killing 17 are Russia’s ‘thanks’ for US diesel sanctions lift, Zelenskyy says
item.description: Overnight strikes on Zaporizhzhia killed at least three children, authorities say.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Turkey bans social media for kids under 15
item.description: The law comes amid a global push for tougher age restrictions on social media platforms.

item.title: [EU Observer] Who really owns Czech Vanadium? Investigators trace possible sanctions-evasion links to Russian oligarch Abramovich’
item.description: Vanadium businesses owned by UAE-based entity appear to be linked with Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich. This has prompted complaints to police about the circumventing of sanctions.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU budget slashed by €159B in new Irish proposal
item.description: The Irish Council presidency's cuts hit competitiveness and development aid, while sparing agriculture and regional funds.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Kann VW gerettet werden? Ein Gespräch mit Olaf Lies
item.description: 50.000 bedrohte Stellen bei Volkswagen stehen als Symbol für eine tiefe Wirtschaftskrise in Niedersachsen und der gesamten Republik. Wie lässt sich der industrielle Kern des Landes retten, bevor die internationale Wettbewerbsfähigkeit endgültig wegbricht? Der niedersächsische SPD-Ministerpräsident Olaf Lies liefert in der Talk-Reihe „Let’s find common ground“ von POLITICO die Bestandsaufnahme einer Industrie am Scheideweg. Im […]

item.title: [DW] Schools crisis in France: Investment fails to inspire confidence
item.description: For weeks, schoolchildren in France have been protesting the failing education system. Compared to many other countries, France invests heavily in education but critics say that the funds are not distributed fairly.

item.title: [DW] Macron and Steinmeier struggle to revive Franco-German ties
item.description: Presidents Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Emmanuel Macron are about to step down from their offices. Their meeting in France made it clear how urgently the Franco-German partnership needs new momentum.

item.title: [DW] Poland: Lifeline for Ukrainian refugees confronts donor fatigue and online abuse as anti-Ukrainian sentiment grows
item.description: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war in her country built a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Now her organization faces donor fatigue, funding cuts and rising hostility as support for Ukrainians in Poland wanes.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia and Herzegovina will soon have a new Grand Mufti
item.description: The new leader of the Islamic Community in Bosnia and Herzegovina will be elected on October 10. The reis-ul-ulema's role is not only important for Muslims in the country itself, but could inspire Muslims across Europe.

item.title: [DW] Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
item.description: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK bans Protestant march from Catholic area in Northern Ireland
item.description: After a 13-day standoff in Portadown, the reversal thrills Irish republicans and enrages Northern Ireland’s unionists, who had hoped to complete a parade blocked since 1998.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Trump lifts sanctions on Russian diesel, suggests US may buy amid surging fuel prices
item.description: The move comes weeks ahead of the midterm election.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ryanair lashes out at Air France and Lufthansa over ownership probe
item.description: The low-cost airline is facing allegations that it violates EU requirements for operating in the bloc.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU trade chief hails ‘crucial first step’ as Beijing talks avoid trade war
item.description: Concessions on electric cars, rare earths and tariffs should be enough for EU and Chinese officials to be able to claim success from trade talks which ended on Friday.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘When you laugh at a dictator, you take away his power’: Artist behind viral naked Trump statue speaks out
item.description: Inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's fairytale, a gold-covered statue of a naked Trump in the halls of European Parliament is meant to make politicians think about democracy, says 'Orange Plague' artist Jens Galschiøt.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU puts 46 more mines and recycling plants on ‘strategic’ list, without closing funding gap
item.description: The EU added 46 strategic minerals projects on Friday, saying progress so far has been ‘very tangible’, but its own figures show little fresh EU financing has materialised.

item.title: [EU Observer] Nato state Montenegro detains top Russian war-blogger Rybar, on suspicion of plotting hybrid tricks (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,688)
item.description: While Rybar’s pro-war editors complain of tightening fronts near Sloviansk, Komar and Dobropillia, independent maps and Ukrainian sources show Moscow’s forces clawing back exaggerated gains as Kyiv tests ambitious advances on the ground and in Russia’s digital backbone.

item.title: [EU Observer] Agrochemical lobbyists are defending a toxic model of agriculture that is heading for collapse
item.description: As pesticide lobbyists dominate a key hearing in Strasbourg, the EU risks locking farmers and citizens into a costly, chemical-dependent food system that poisons water, fuels disease and drains billions in EU subsidies away from real sustainable farming.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: What would a coalition of right and far-right in Spain mean for Europe?
item.description: Spain is heading for early elections, after Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap vote last week. According to current polls, the conservative People's Party, or PP, is ahead of Sánchez's Socialists, while Vox is also making significant gains. What would happen if they governed together?

item.title: [EU Observer] Orbán channelled public money into propaganda through Hungarian billionaire Lőrinc Mészáros (Day 150 of the Tisza government)
item.description: Internal documents show how a top Orbán-era rail contractor showered Megafon influencers with billions of forints.

item.title: [EU Observer] Video game industry believes EU Kids Act will drive small creators and old games into extinction
item.description: Campaigners have warned that stringent requirements to adapt games to children by default would prompt the extinction of small games and make costs spiral for developers.

item.title: [EU Observer] French kitchenware giant Tefal faces legal ultimatum over harmful chemicals, as Europeans’ health at stake
item.description: Environmental NGOs have threatened to sue the owner of Tefal, a leading French kitchenware company, over failing to phase out forever chemicals from their products, at a high price for consumer health.
